\subsection{Voltammetric Electrode Model}\label{ss:analog-electrode-bc}

This section documents a \emph{simulation model}, not a circuit block and not
silicon: a Verilog-A element standing in for the electrode--electrolyte
interface when a bench sweeps potential and expects a voltammetric peak.

A linear network cannot produce one: its extrema stay pinned at the switching
potentials whatever the element values (Figure~\ref{fig:electrode-validation},
dashed). A peak needs Butler--Volmer kinetics, exponential in overpotential
about \(E^{0\prime}\), together with diffusional depletion, which turns the
exponential rise into a \(t^{-1/2}\) decay; kinetics alone give a sigmoid.

The faradaic current is Butler--Volmer in heterogeneous-rate-constant form,
emitted anodic-positive to match the transimpedance amplifier:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:electrode-bv}
  i_f \;=\; nFA\,k^{0}\!\left[\,C_R(0,t)\,
      e^{\,(1-\alpha)\,n f\,(E-E^{0\prime})}
    \;-\; C_O(0,t)\,
      e^{\,-\alpha\,n f\,(E-E^{0\prime})}\right],
  \qquad f = \frac{F}{RT},
\end{equation}
both exponents clamped at \(\pm\)\texttt{expmax} through \(\mathrm{limexp}\).
Surface concentrations follow diffusion into a finite Nernst layer,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:electrode-fick}
  \frac{\partial C_s}{\partial t} \;=\; D\,
  \frac{\partial^{2} C_s}{\partial x^{2}},
  \qquad s \in \{O, R\},
\end{equation}
with flux set by \(i_f\) at the surface and bulk pinned at the layer edge,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:electrode-bc}
  D\!\left.\frac{\partial C_O}{\partial x}\right|_{x=0} = +\frac{i_f}{nFA},
  \qquad
  D\!\left.\frac{\partial C_R}{\partial x}\right|_{x=0} = -\frac{i_f}{nFA},
  \qquad
  C_s(\delta, t) = C_s^{*}.
\end{equation}
The simulator solves the finite-volume form of \eqref{eq:electrode-fick} on an
expanding grid of 28 slabs per species,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:electrode-box}
  h_j\,\frac{\mathrm{d} C_j}{\mathrm{d} t}
  \;=\; \frac{D}{d_{j-1}}\left(C_{j-1}-C_j\right)
   \;-\; \frac{D}{d_j}\left(C_j-C_{j+1}\right),
  \qquad h_j = h_0\,\beta^{\,j},
\end{equation}
with \(h_0 = \SI{0.5}{\micro\metre}\), \(\beta = 1.280\) and
\(\delta = \SI{1.79}{\milli\metre}\). Each slab is one electrical node carrying
its concentration scaled by \SI{1e-6}{\mole\per\cubic\centi\metre}, since the
raw value solves to noise below the simulator's voltage tolerance. Parameters
are in Table~\ref{tab:electrode-params}, in the CGS units of the source
literature.

Benches instantiate it as the cell of Figure~\ref{fig:randles-cell} with the
charge-transfer branch replaced by this element. Only voltammetry needs it; the
linear cell remains correct for small-signal impedance work.
